scope: Exact acquired 85-page arXiv v2, full primary text reading; targeted actual page-image inspection and independent calculations distinguished.

sections.work: Nonsymmetric Nash system, large-N rather than all-N claims; distinction between D and L semimonotonicity; positive idiosyncratic diffusion and common-noise scope; heterogeneous subsequential limits rather than unrestricted full-sequence uniqueness.

Euclidean vector and Frobenius matrix norms, nonsymmetric quadratic-form order, J=J_N tensor I_d, empirical and weighted norms, Wasserstein metrics; these conventions are operative in Problems 3,5,6,7.

D/L definitions, pointwise mixed derivatives, MF individual and row/column estimates, DS/LS smallness, H0/H1/H1prime, uniform own-state/label conditions, S and LP, Theorems3.8/3.12/3.17 and exact rate regime. Problems2,6 concern literal assumptions/auxiliary claims. Reverse sufficiency suggested in Remark3.3 has not been independently proved or disproved and is not reported as a defect.

Unweighted reflection estimate versus game-specific weighted doubling argument; mean-field first/second/third derivative scales; boundedness and smoothing; constants exp(c/sigma) and double exponential. Independent drift example separates false general extension from the original Nash lemma. No author-code computations.

D bootstrap, small terminal/running semimonotonicity and large N, synchronous stochastic comparison, N^-1/2 error, fixed-N continuity extension. These conditions exclude the intended-definition version of Problem2's example.

L bootstrap and diagonal lower bound, Riccati/energy controls, sigma dependence, use of global versus pointwise semimonotonicity. No independent replacement proof for every bootstrap estimate is claimed.

Label estimates, terminal data, parameter-space compactness, empirical Wp coupling, q>4 to P2 approximation, full versus leave-one-out measures, bounded moment truncation, continuous disintegration and finitely many populations, representation and classical PDE for positive time. Exact examples and repairs for Problems3-5,8; major finite-population conclusions not declared false from auxiliary errors.

Joint limit sigma_N->0, liminf sigma_N log log N threshold, propagation of semimonotonicity, gradient estimate8.4 and its dependence on false generic drift extension. Forcing bounds alone do not supply the missing weighted drift argument. Intended theorem not refuted by arbitrary drift.

General-Hamiltonian differentiated system, H0-H1/H1prime roles, operator versus quadratic-form/Frobenius bounds, semimonotonicity propagation. Local matrix corrections in Problem6; no general-Hamiltonian theorem counterexample established.

Fixed-N heat contraction, bounded smooth data, global continuation using derivative/value bounds, signs of forward dynamics and representation, Hamiltonian offset dependence, J eigenvalue multiplicity and Duhamel time arguments.
Weighted parabolic barrier, positive sigma, beta>=0, N-independent weighted trace and 1/3 time modulus. No additional substantive issue established.
References identified. External regularity/propagation-of-chaos/optimal-transport results not individually reproved. Findings use self-contained counterexamples, not unverifiable reference claims.

independent_checks.method: Exact analytic arguments, SymPy identities, 80-working-digit mpmath root and quadrature corroboration
independent_checks.limitations: No interval certification; finite numerics do not prove universal assertions. No PDE simulation or author code execution.

assumption_boundaries: All counterexamples use the stated norm and matrix conventions.
Problem1 addresses the proposed arbitrary-drift extension; actual Nash-gradient structure may permit repair.
Problem2 distinguishes literal (3.9) from corrected Definition3.1; all data are bounded C-infinity.
Problem3 uses explicit exact Nash solutions and LS=0, not an arbitrary drift family.
Problem4 applies the lemma's arbitrary bounded Lipschitz drift class and all-label quantifier.
Problem5 includes the label component of joint Wasserstein distance and arbitrarily large odd N.
Problem6 does not assume mixed Jacobians symmetric when the source does not.
Problem7 permits positive constant Hamiltonian shifts and satisfies both semimonotonicity alternatives.
Problem8 uses the arbitrary metric-space quantifier; the actual application space is separable.
